evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Arden says 'it might take around ten to fifteen minutes ma'am. Will that be fine?' and gets affirmation, but never frames the value promise ('quote you can depend on') or waits for an explicit yes to proceed — moves into probing immediately after confirmation.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Arden asks for moving date (Oct 23rd), property type (2070 sq ft three-story townhome), and bedrooms (3 bed), but does not explicitly ask for city-to-city route or approximate size estimate upfront in Section 1. Size emerges later through property description, not as a direct discovery question.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Arden asks 'aside from the pricing, is there any move concern that you need to, that you need us to be aware of' but only after already mentioning the 10–15 minute time frame and beginning to collect details. Customer responds with reassurance ('you all were great last time'), not a concern, so no actual concerns are raised to follow up on.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: No concerns were raised by the customer, so this is N/A, but the rep did not use this section to probe deeper into what matters to the customer.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: Rep does not reflect back or summarize what was heard. Customer says 'we just want help with the big items' and 'we have three days to move,' but Arden does not confirm understanding with a summary like 'So what I'm hearing is...'
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Arden gathers property type (townhome, 2070 sq ft, 3 story), bedroom count (3), and partial room inventory through the itemized list (king bed, queen bed, dresser, TV stand, sectional, chairs, hutch, kitchen table, garage items). Missing: explicit walking distance, floor layout clarity, additional stops, and special considerations. The item list is detailed but reactive to customer initiation, not proactive logistics probing.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Arden asks 'how about boxes? Are we going to move boxes?' partway through the inventory conversation.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Arden never asks 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?' — only confirms whether boxes will be moved by the customer.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Arden gives a range: 'I'm estimating the move to take only around two and a half to three and a half hours estimate. So budget thing that if they'll be able to go within three and a half hours, that's around $777.' This includes both a time range and a price anchor ($777). However, it is not personalized to this customer's concerns or stated prep level — it's a generic calculation based on item count and distance, not tied to the customer's anxiety about extension availability or her prior experience with the last move.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Arden mentions '2.5 hours' as minimum and states 'no deposit required, no upfront payment. You only pay after the actual move was done,' which covers one element of fee transparency. However, trip fees, overnight fees, packing materials, and the '15-minute increments' commitment are never mentioned. The '2.5-hour minimum' framing is present but incomplete.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Arden never asks 'Does that feel fair?' or any variant. After quoting $777, the conversation immediately pivots to availability windows and the customer asks 'what's the Max we can have them that day?' — no pricing affirmation check.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Sections 5 (Two Promises) are not delivered, so there is nothing to close the loop on.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Arden never asks a genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or equivalent. The call ends with logistical confirmation and a callback plan, with no re-check for remaining concerns.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Arden never asks 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Arden never asks 'Would you like our help with your move?' or any explicit ask for the business. Instead, the rep says 'Well, what we normally do if you want ma'am so that we can have this truck reserved for you I can go ahead and book a confirmation' and lets the customer decide ('let me talk this over with my husband'). The customer then says 'go ahead and book me for three and a half today and then I'll call back,' but Arden does not explicitly ask for the booking — it is offered as a logistics option, not a direct ask for the business.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Arden confirms the date (Oct 23rd / Friday), email (D.C.Bell@comcast.net), estimated hours (3.5 hours initially, with note to call back to adjust), and crew size (2 movers implied from prior discussion). Missing: arrival window specificity, exact phone number confirmation for callback, full address confirmation for the destination townhome, and crew notes about the customer's concerns (extension availability, same-city move).

top_strength: Arden skillfully managed a complex repeat-customer scenario by listening to the customer's constraints (three-day window, minimal crew needed, proximity of the move) and adapting the estimate conversation to focus on itemized inventory rather than forcing a generic property-size quote.
coaching_note: Section 5 (Two Promises — On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage) and Section 6 (final concerns recheck) were completely skipped; prioritize delivering both before routing to callback, and always end with an explicit ask for the business ('Would you like our help with your move?') rather than letting the customer volunteer to book.
